_comment: SSOT for the /fertility-preserving-surgery/ pillar guide. tiers[] seeds the hero comparison + ItemList JSON-LD. conditions[] seeds the per-condition rows; citationsHtml carries inline /library/ links rendered with set:html. Slugs verified in docs/research/2026-06-13-fertility-preserving-surgery-evidence.md. PCOS leads with RRM wedge resection as the restorative best approach; drilling is the destructive lesser approach and is not platformed. v2 2026-06-13: tubal expanded, Asherman's + adenomyosis + cesarean scar added, adhesions deepened. v3 2026-06-14: male reproductive surgery added (varicocele; obstruction/vasectomy reversal) per Dr. Whittaker, restore-the-cause vs bypass-with-ICSI framing.

tiers.label: Restorative reproductive (RRM) surgery
tiers.goal: Remove the disease and leave the reproductive organs more functional than before.
hallmarks: Complete excision or removal of disease
Deliberate adhesion prevention with technique and barriers
Treats the root cause, not only the symptoms

tiers.label: Specialist surgery
tiers.goal: Remove the disease competently. The specialty is treating the disease, not preserving fertility.
hallmarks: Skilled at removing the disease (excision, myomectomy, cystectomy)
Fertility preservation is not the focus of the specialty
Reconstruction and restorative steps are applied inconsistently, if at all
Adhesion prevention is often not part of the treatment, or not known
tiers.fertilityImpact: Often preserved, but not the aim
tiers.whoPerformsIt: Skilled gynecologic surgeons focused on the disease

tiers.label: Conventional surgery
tiers.goal: Control symptoms, with fertility a lower priority.
hallmarks: Ablation or destruction of tissue rather than restorative removal
Technique that can deplete ovarian reserve
Default removal of an organ where conservation was possible
tiers.whoPerformsIt: A general approach where fertility is not the goal

conditions.name: Endometriosis
conditions.tier1: Wide excision of disease with reconstruction and adhesion prevention, including laser excision when used to clear disease from fallopian tubes with minimal thermal damage, with histology confirming complete removal.
conditions.tier2: Excision by a surgeon focused on removing the disease, with adhesion prevention and reconstruction often left out.
conditions.tier3: Ablation or fulguration of the surface, which can leave deeper disease behind.
conditions.citationsHtml: Complete excision without mandatory hormonal suppression; reproductive capacity and recurrence after surgery.

conditions.name: Ovarian cysts and endometriomas
conditions.tier1: Tissue-conserving removal that takes out the cyst while sparing healthy ovary and conserving the ovary itself.
conditions.tier2: Cystectomy focused on removing the cyst, with less attention to sparing healthy ovarian tissue.
conditions.tier3: Aggressive stripping, or removing the ovary, when conservation was possible.
conditions.citationsHtml: the timing and technique of endometrioma excision; a long-life approach to preserving reproductive integrity.

conditions.name: PCOS (ovarian wedge resection)
conditions.tier1: RRM ovarian wedge resection: meticulous microsurgical reduction of androgen-producing stroma that restores spontaneous ovulation and durable hormonal normalization.
conditions.tier2: Wedge resection performed without the full restorative microsurgical technique.
conditions.tier3: Destructive ovarian surgery, such as drilling or diathermy, that ablates ovarian tissue rather than restoring it.
conditions.citationsHtml: hormonal normalization after wedge resection; durable long-term outcomes; restored ovulation and conception.

conditions.name: Fibroids
conditions.tier1: Myomectomy that removes fibroids and conserves the uterus for a future pregnancy.
conditions.tier2: Myomectomy with less attention to reconstruction or adhesion prevention.
conditions.tier3: Hysterectomy in a woman whose uterus could have been conserved.
conditions.citationsHtml: myomectomy as a reproductive procedure; fertility enhancement and preservation.

conditions.name: Tubal disease
conditions.tier1: Selective HSG or tubal cannulation for proximal occlusion; laparoscopic fimbrioplasty or salpingostomy for distal disease; microsurgical anastomosis when indicated: evaluation precedes every decision.
conditions.tier2: Tubal surgery without microsurgical assessment of mucosal integrity, or referral for bypass before reconstruction has been offered.
conditions.tier3: Bilateral salpingectomy recommended as the only option without first assessing whether the tubes are reconstructable.
conditions.citationsHtml: Nolan & Whittaker, Tuboplasty (2026); McEwen, reconstructive tubal surgery; reconstructive tubal microsurgery; assessing which tubes are reconstructable.

conditions.name: Asherman's syndrome
conditions.tier1: Hysteroscopic lysis of intrauterine adhesions, followed by endometrial optimization: intrauterine estradiol, adhesion barriers such as Interceed, and endometrial cultures or biopsy to address underlying pathology.
conditions.tier2: Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis without systematic endometrial optimization or adhesion-barrier placement.
conditions.tier3: No operative intervention, or expectant management that accepts a scarred cavity without attempting restoration.
conditions.citationsHtml: Hysteroscopic lysis and endometrial optimization: see intrauterine adhesions (Asherman's syndrome) in the glossary; PRP is an emerging adjunct studied for thin or scarred endometrium.

conditions.name: Adenomyosis (focal)
conditions.tier1: Uterine-sparing adenomyomectomy: surgical removal of focal adenomyosis from the uterine wall with reconstruction, preserving the uterus for future pregnancy.
conditions.tier2: Hormonal suppression of symptoms without addressing the focal disease surgically.
conditions.tier3: Hysterectomy where the disease was focal and uterine conservation was possible.
conditions.citationsHtml: Focal adenomyosis and uterine-sparing adenomyomectomy: see adenomyosis in the glossary; a fertility-preserving adenomyomectomy with myometrial reconstruction relieved symptoms and preserved fertility potential.

conditions.name: Cesarean scar and fertility-friendly cesarean
conditions.tier1: Isthmocele repair for an established niche; and a prevention-first mindset at every cesarean: non-inclusion of the endometrium in closure, double-layer closure, non-locking stitches, and peritoneal closure.
conditions.tier2: Standard cesarean technique without deliberate niche-prevention steps; isthmocele repaired only if symptomatic.
conditions.tier3: No attention to scar architecture or niche prevention; isthmocele left unaddressed even when it impairs implantation.
conditions.citationsHtml: See uterine isthmocele (cesarean scar defect) in the glossary and the isthmocele guide; closure location and technique are the main determinants of hysterotomy healing; isthmocele can impair fertility and is addressed by repair.

conditions.name: Pelvic adhesions
conditions.tier1: Microsurgical handling, minimizing blood on the surgical field, physiologic irrigation (lactated Ringer's), peritoneal closure as an active adhesion barrier, and barrier membranes (Gore-Tex/ePTFE or Interceed) placed before closing.
conditions.tier2: Competent disease removal, with adhesion prevention applied inconsistently or not at all.
conditions.tier3: Little attention to adhesion prevention, accepting reformation as inevitable.

conditions.name: Varicocele
conditions.tier1: Microsurgical subinguinal varicocelectomy, or varicocele embolization as a minimally invasive alternative, to correct the most common reversible cause of male infertility and move semen parameters back toward natural conception: technique determines the outcome.
conditions.tier2: Varicocele ligation performed competently but without microsurgical technique, where higher recurrence and hydrocele rates are accepted and fertility restoration is not the organizing aim.
conditions.tier3: Proceeding directly to IVF-ICSI for a clinically significant, correctable varicocele without first offering repair.
conditions.citationsHtml: a comprehensive andrological workup restored natural fertility in 40.9% of couples seeking natural conception; microsurgical repair carries the highest fertility rates and lowest complication rates; recurrence varies with technique from 0% to 35%. See also quantified varicocele-repair outcomes and microsurgical varicocelectomy technique.

conditions.name: Obstruction and vasectomy reversal
conditions.tier1: Microsurgical reconstruction: vasovasostomy or vasoepididymostomy for vasal or epididymal obstruction, and transurethral resection of the ejaculatory duct for ejaculatory-duct obstruction, returning sperm to the ejaculate so natural conception becomes possible.
conditions.tier2: Surgical sperm retrieval (TESE, PESA, or MESA) performed competently, but as a direct feeder to ICSI, without first assessing whether reconstruction could restore natural fertility.
conditions.tier3: Defaulting to sperm retrieval and ICSI, or to donor sperm, for a reconstructable obstruction without evaluating whether reconnection could restore natural fertility.
conditions.citationsHtml: treating the cause rather than bypassing it restored natural fertility in male-factor couples; surgical techniques to restore sperm delivery versus retrieval for IVF-ICSI. See also vasectomy reversal succeeds in around 60 to 80% of cases and the range of surgical options for male infertility.
